title: Threads, Chrome, Air, Alpha & Atomic Moves
description: An image unravelled into ribbons, a CSS-declared title bar, CJK inter-script air, one colour token as every state, and a DOM move that preserves state.

drops.title: Unwoven Threads
drops.description: Each card is sliced into independent horizontal ribbons that slide, gap, whiten and vanish as it drifts away from centre.
drops.concept: Clément Grellier's Codrops piece splits each image card into 26 ribbons — separate geometry rather than one subdivided plane, so each band moves without dragging its neighbours. A 'tear' value of 0 at screen centre rising to 1 at the edges drives a per-ribbon random slide, a widening gap and a whitening fade so nothing leaves a coloured ghost. Rebuilt here as five procedurally painted canvases with a drawImage band per ribbon, plus scroll, manual and drift tear sources.
drops.source: Clément Grellier — “Unwoven: Building an Infinite Loom” on Codrops, 5 Sep 2026

interaction.mouse: Scroll the strip sideways — cards tear as they leave the centre; the panel sliders retune ribbon count, slide distance, curve and whitening.
interaction.click: Switch the tear source between Scroll, Manual and Drift.
interaction.touch: Swipe the strip; snap points hold a card at centre so it re-weaves itself.

drops.title: App Chrome Regions
drops.description: Three desktop-app mockups lay out their own title bars with window-drag: move — and every control inside has to opt back out.
drops.concept: Chrome 152 standardises the old non-standard -webkit-app-region as window-drag, renaming its values to move and none and giving it explicit inheritance. That inheritance is the trap: declare a custom title bar draggable and every button, input and traffic light inside it inherits the region, so a click-and-drag on 'play' flings the window instead. An x-ray mode tints the move region green and each no-drag island red, and an in-page fallback drags the mock window using the identical rules.
drops.source: The window-drag property in the Chrome 152 release notes

interaction.mouse: Drag a title bar to move the window; the opted-out controls stay clickable instead.
interaction.click: Toggle x-ray, extend the drag region into the body, hide the no-drag islands, or snap to a 16px grid.
interaction.touch: Same drag rules under touch; on narrow screens the windows arrive as a cascade with every title bar exposed.

drops.title: Inter-Script Air
drops.description: The sliver of space between Han, kana or Hangul and adjacent Latin — via text-autospace, a tunable polyfill, or nothing at all.
drops.concept: When alphanumerics land in a run of CJK, good typesetting inserts a small gap: the Chinese and Japanese layout requirements say up to a ¼em, the CSS spec offers ⅛em as the smaller alternative. text-autospace finally asks the browser to do it, but support is patchy and inconsistent, so this drop puts the native property, a run-tokenising manual polyfill and no spacing at all side by side across four samples, with live boundary counts and rendered widths.
drops.source: W3C Internationalization — “Managing inline spaces in Chinese & Japanese”

interaction.mouse: Drag the gap slider from 1/16em to ¼em and watch the rendered width and line count move with it.
interaction.click: Switch between off, manual and native spacing; tint the inserted gaps; toggle text-spacing-trim.
interaction.touch: The panel stacks above the samples on narrow screens; every control is tap-sized.

drops.title: Alpha Ladder
drops.description: CSS Color 5's alpha() keeps every channel of an origin colour and changes only opacity — so five interaction states become five rungs on one token.
drops.concept: Relative alpha colours shipped in Chrome 152: alpha(from var(--brand) / 40%) preserves the origin colour's components and rewrites nothing but transparency. Rest, hover, press, focus ring and disabled all descend from a single --brand token, so dragging one hue slider re-derives an entire control surface at once. The sheet layers three tiers — alpha(), then rgb(from … r g b / α), then color-mix() — and the panel reports which one the browser actually took.
drops.source: The alpha() colour function on MDN Web Docs

interaction.mouse: Hover and press the buttons, chips, rows, switches and field — every state is one alpha rung away from the same token.
interaction.click: Latch chips, flip switches, fire the token-tinted ripple; the sliders retune hue, chroma, lightness and the hover/press/ring alphas.
interaction.touch: Press states double as touch feedback; the panel moves inline above the surfaces on narrow screens.

drops.title: Atomic Move List
drops.description: insertBefore() detaches every node it moves — iframes reload, animations restart, focus and scroll vanish. moveBefore() does not.
drops.concept: Reordering a list the classic way is an implicit remove-then-insert, and the browser treats a detached node as gone: iframes re-run, CSS animations restart from zero, focus and caret are lost, inner scroll offsets snap back. moveBefore() relocates the node atomically and keeps all of it. Each card here carries a self-timing iframe, a nine-second animation, a scrolled list and a focusable input, and a live scoreboard counts exactly what each operation preserved.
drops.source: Bramus Van Damme on moveBefore — now an Interop 2026 focus area

interaction.mouse: Scroll a card's inner list and focus its input, then reorder in both modes and read the scoreboard.
interaction.click: Move cards up and down, shuffle, rotate or reverse the whole list; switch between insertBefore and moveBefore.
interaction.touch: All reordering is button-driven, so it works identically under touch.
